summary: ZephyrInsurance inter-tenant context bleed during cluster maintenance — urgent remediation and post-incident audit
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled maintenance window on 2026-03-10 for a control-plane kernel migration, a replication edge-case caused in-memory KV entries belonging to one tenant to be served to a different tenant's inference stream. Impact: Potential PII exposure across 3 sessions for ZephyrInsurance and another enterprise tenant; streaming responses contained short prompt fragments from unrelated accounts. This ticket tracks the incident timeline, mitigation, customer communication, and required follow-up audits.

Environment: Hosted API, production, us-east-1 region, serving-runtime v2.14.1, control-plane migration job #cp-migrate-20260310.

Immediate impact: Customer-facing streaming completions returned mixed-context fragments for a subset of requests between 2026-03-10T03:22Z and 2026-03-10T03:46Z. Affected traffic routed through GPU pool rp-us-east-1-gpu-4.

Preserved artifacts: request IDs, truncated response payloads, routing logs, control-plane migration logs, raft replication debug traces, and temporary capture of affected sessions.
impact: 3 customer sessions returned fragments of other customers' prompts; estimated 9 unique prompt fragments leaked across tenants; no persisted artifacts found in object storage or audit log buckets after initial checks; ZephyrInsurance classified leaked fragments as potentially containing customer PII (policy numbers).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Triggered during control-plane migration job cp-migrate-20260310 with rolling restarts of routing agents.
2) Simultaneous KV flush + in-flight streaming requests hit a race in replica promotion codepath.
3) Requests routed to a newly promoted replica that had a stale in-memory prefix table, causing short prefix fragments to be appended to outgoing streams.
logs: See attached snippets in the ticket: routing.log (2026-03-10T03:20-03:50), raft-debug.log (promotion events at 03:21:45Z), streaming-traces.log (3 affected request_ids). Relevant Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01SUPPORT/p1678464000000.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): validated customer report and isolated affected request IDs; paused all maintenance ops and disabled rolling promotion for remaining nodes.
SRE early findings: a race in replica-promotion path allowed a pending in-memory prefix buffer to be read by a newly elected leader during a narrow window (~25s).
Repro attempts: deterministic repro required synthetic race harness and the exact maintenance timing; not reproducible on staging without forcing replica preemption and manual buffer flush delay.
Related code area: replica_promotion.go (promotionBufferFlush), serving-runtime cache code path that merges prefix entries into outgoing chunk streams.
Telemetry: no evidence of persisted cross-tenant data in S3 audit logs; leakage appears limited to in-memory streaming buffers only.
mitigation: 1) Rollback: rolled back control-plane migration and stopped agent promotions; 2) Immediate hotfix deployed to zero-out in-memory prefix buffers on leader promotion (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/11892); 3) Disabled streaming prefix merging for multi-tenant pools until patch validated; 4) Notified ZephyrInsurance and other potentially affected tenant with request IDs and offer to run customer-side audit.
resolution: Hotfix applied (serving v2.14.2-hotfix1) and validated by synthetic harness and live canary traffic. No additional leaks observed after 2026-03-10T04:05Z. Customer accepted the immediate remediation and requested formal audit. Incident declared resolved after three 24-hour clean checks of streaming traces and audit buckets.
follow_up_actions: 1) Post-incident security audit for all multi-tenant GPU pools (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-20).
2) Add automated leader-promotion invariant tests to CI (owner: infra-team, due 2026-03-17).
3) Expand streaming telemetry retention for 30 days for enterprise tenants to assist future forensics (owner: observability, due 2026-04-01).
4) Update maintenance runbook: require two-step fence-and-flush before promotions (owner: ops, due 2026-03-15).
5) Customer compensation & review: CS to coordinate with Finance for a one-month credit and schedule an executive review meeting (owner: CS, due 2026-03-18).
